opportunities.name: arXiv topic search → Semantic Scholar citation count → save to Notes
opportunities.description: For a given research topic, subject category and year, run an arXiv advanced title search, take the top result, look up its citation count on Semantic Scholar, and add a note in the format '<topic> (<year>): <title> by <first author>, <N> citations'.
steps: Open arxiv.org and go to Search > Advanced Search
Type the topic into the search term field (field = Title)
Tick the subject category checkbox
Choose 'Specific year' and enter the year
Click Search and take the first result's arXiv ID and title
Open semanticscholar.org, reject cookies if asked, search the exact paper title
Read the citation count and first author from the matching result
Open Notes and add a new note: '<topic> (<year>): <title> by <first author>, <citations> citations'

instances.values: topic='retrieval augmented generation', category=Computer Science, year=2023 → RIGHT: Retrieval-augmented Generation for Mainstream Hashtag Recommendation, Run-Ze Fan, 11 citations
topic='protein structure diffusion', category=Quantitative Biology, year=2024 → Accelerating Inference in Molecular Diffusion Models..., Ian Dunn, 7 citations

opportunities.name: Court case lookup → related statute on LII → save to Notes
opportunities.description: For a given Supreme Court case, find it on CourtListener to get the U.S. Reports citation and decision date, look up a related U.S. Code section on Cornell LII to get its title, and add a note in the format '<case>: <citation>, decided <date>. See <statute> (<section title>)'.
steps: Open courtlistener.com (click the logo to get back to the home search)
Type the case name into the keyword search and click Search
Open the matching Supreme Court opinion and read the citation (e.g. 585 U.S. 296) and the decision date
Open law.cornell.edu and type the statute citation into the site search
Read the title of the first result (the section heading)
Open Notes and add: '<case>: <citation>, decided <date>. See <statute> (<section title>)'
